record.paper_title: Progress on homogeneous Einstein manifolds and some open probrems
record.context_brief: Equivalent isotropy summands and Stiefel manifolds
record.original_question: For Stiefel manifolds such as V_k R^n = SO(n)/SO(n-k), and more generally homogeneous spaces G/K whose isotropy representation contains equivalent summands, is the set of invariant Einstein metrics finite, or can continuous one-parameter families of invariant Einstein metrics occur?

evidence.quote: one-parameter families of invariant Einstein metrics

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G/K$ be a compact homogeneous space, where $G$ is a compact connected Lie group and $K\subset G$ is a closed subgroup, with reductive decomposition $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{k}\oplus\mathfrak{m}$ (so that $\mathrm{Ad}(K)\mathfrak{m}\subset\mathfrak{m}$). A Riemannian metric on $G/K$ is called $G$-invariant if it is induced by an $\mathrm{Ad}(K)$-invariant inner product on $\mathfrak{m}$. An invariant Einstein metric is a $G$-invariant Riemannian metric whose Ricci tensor is a constant multiple of the metric. Suppose that the isotropy representation $\mathfrak{m}=\mathfrak{m}_1\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{m}_s$ of $K$ decomposes into irreducible $\mathrm{Ad}(K)$-submodules among which at least two are equivalent as $K$-representations.

A distinguished family of such spaces are the real Stiefel manifolds $V_k(\mathbb{R}^n)=\mathrm{SO}(n)/\mathrm{SO}(n-k)$ of orthonormal $k$-frames in $\mathbb{R}^n$, whose isotropy representation contains equivalent summands whenever $k\ge 2$.

Determine, modulo homothety, whether the set of $G$-invariant Einstein metrics on such a homogeneous space $G/K$ (and in particular on $V_k(\mathbb{R}^n)$) is necessarily finite, or whether continuous one-parameter families of non-isometric $G$-invariant Einstein metrics can occur.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., Arvanitoyeorgos–Sakane–Statha and others, 2014–2021) has produced new families of invariant Einstein metrics on Stiefel manifolds $V_k(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and on related spaces with equivalent isotropy summands, typically by restricting to a smaller invariance group to make the Einstein system tractable. However, no general classification or finiteness theorem is known in the presence of equivalent isotropy summands, and the question of whether continuous one-parameter families of invariant Einstein metrics can occur on such spaces remains open.

status_evidence.title: Homogeneous Einstein metrics on Stiefel manifolds associated to flag manifolds with two isotropy summands
status_evidence.snippet: For 2 ≤ p ≤ (2/5)n−1, V_{2p}R^n admits at least four invariant Einstein metrics determined by Ad(U(p)×SO(n-2p))-invariant scalar products.
status_evidence.claim: Recent results produce new invariant Einstein metrics on Stiefel manifolds, but do not resolve the finiteness vs. one-parameter family question in general.

status_evidence.title: New homogeneous Einstein metrics on Stiefel manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of new SO(n)-invariant Einstein metrics on V_k R^n using reduced invariance.
status_evidence.claim: The structure of all invariant Einstein metrics on Stiefel manifolds remains incompletely understood due to equivalent isotropy summands.
